answer: Every dune is a fake identity. Registration is anchored at the inlet: each new dune is compared with every dune already anchored and with every other new dune in its batch, so duplicates collide there. Each comparison costs one terrace, one pairwise audit by an independent judge. The kth dune pays k−1 terrace; fielding k copies pays k(k−1)/2 terrace, and parallel copies cannot skip a pair. Call this pair-checked registration. It breaks if an auditor certifies a comparison after seeing only one dune.
